messages.subject: qtl for Mac OS X 10.3.x
parts:
Howdy. I'm very new to R so please pardon the ignorance. The
install.packages("qtl") command goes something like this:

install.packages("qtl")
trying URL `http://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/PACKAGES'
Content type `text/plain; charset=iso-8859-1' length 51514 bytes
opened URL
==================================================
downloaded 50Kb

trying URL `http://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/qtl_0.98-57.tar.gz'
Content type `application/x-tar' length 424152 bytes
opened URL
==================================================
downloaded 414Kb

* Installing *source* package 'qtl' ...
** libs
/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/bin/SHLIB: line 1: make:
command not found
** Removing
'/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/2.0.1/Resources/library/qtl'
** Restoring previous
'/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/2.0.1/Resources/library/qtl'
ERROR: compilation failed for package 'qtl'

Delete downloaded files (y/N)? y

Warning message:
Installation of package qtl had non-zero exit status in:
install.packages("qtl")

The installed package does not work (for example, it does not recognize
the "read.cross" command and help("qtl") produces a blank page). If I
choose "N" at the above "Delete downloaded files (y/N)?" prompt I get
identical results. What's going on?
Much thanks,
Dave

messages.author: f388084a0de67b60
messages.subject: Re: qtl for Mac OS X 10.3.x
parts:
I would recommend installing the binary version. To install from
source,
you're going to need to put together some further tools.

See if the attached file works for you.

karl

messages.author: ab8dbe3bec292afe
messages.subject: Re: qtl for Mac OS X 10.3.x
parts:
Try to download the file without unzipping it. The file should be in
.tgz format, which you can install directly from R, clicking on
"Packages & Data" -> "Package Installer" -> "Local binary package".

Try downloading it directly from the following:

http://www.biostat.jhsph.edu/~kbroman/software/qtl/qtl_0.98-57.tgz

karl

messages.author: 42ba0ee8d412218f
messages.subject: Re: qtl for Mac OS X 10.3.x
parts:
Yu need to call the "package" within R before running any of the R/qtl
commands/functions.
Do:

>library(qtl)
